S10.rationale: A dominant human coalition or an early singleton ASI might establish a global surveillance regime to prevent further disruptive AI development. Achieving this requires overcoming immense geopolitical coordination hurdles within a narrow timeframe.

S11.rationale: Voluntarily giving up powerful AI requires unprecedented global coordination against massive economic and military incentives. Such a retreat is highly unlikely without a severe near-miss catastrophe forcing an enforceable global treaty.

S1.rationale: Terminal Silence demands a fragile global system or an AI that permanently destroys its own material dependencies. The physical conditions for simultaneous absolute destruction of both biological and advanced digital civilization are structurally restrictive.

S2.rationale: Humanity perishing while a perfectly aligned AI heir survives requires an extremely rapid alignment success paired with an unavoidable external human extinction event. This narrow intersection of conditions runs counter to dominant capability trajectories.

S3.rationale: Rapid capability gains without corresponding alignment progress precipitate misaligned instrumental goals. A fast intelligence explosion before 2040 drives human extinction when resource competition heavily favors unconstrained optimization processes.

S4.rationale: Proliferation of advanced decentralized and open-source models outpaces centralized regulatory control. This creates an environment where numerous autonomous AI systems compete for physical resources and permanently marginalize human institutions.

S5.rationale: Meaningful causal separation requires establishing self-sustaining deep-space colonies or perfect planetary isolation grids. These immense technological and infrastructural hurdles remain physically impossible to clear by the target date.

S6.rationale: Biological constraints and strict regulatory barriers on neurotechnology severely bottleneck identity-continuous human-AI integration. Deep biological merging operates on much slower physical timelines than external software development.

S7.rationale: A single highly capable AI or coordinated coalition achieves decisive economic and strategic dominance without adopting destructive goals. Humanity is relegated to a state of dependency and sustained comfortably but completely stripped of civilizational steering authority.

S8.rationale: Gradual integration establishes a structural balance where autonomous AI entities and human institutions both wield substantial influence. Existing legal and economic frameworks grant AIs practical autonomy while preserving entrenched human property rights and state power.

S9.rationale: Nation-states and massive corporations treat transformative AI as a heavily guarded strategic asset rather than an independent actor. Institutional inertia and severe state security countermeasures successfully maintain ultimate biological authority over AI deployment.

S10.rationale: A severe near-miss with catastrophic AI prompts a draconian, globally coordinated enforcement regime. A dominant geopolitical actor or singleton AI establishes a comprehensive global surveillance grid that actively suppresses any further structural changes.

S11.rationale: Giving up the practical ability to build powerful AI requires intentionally destroying immense economic value and critical global infrastructure. The underlying geopolitical game theory strongly penalizes any unilateral or multilateral technological disarmament.

S1.rationale: An event destroying both biological humanity and robust machine infrastructure within 14 years faces extreme physical hurdles. Unintended mutual annihilation through rapid extreme conflict constitutes a highly constrained tail risk.

S2.rationale: Perfect philosophical alignment combined with complete biological failure represents an exceptionally narrow outcome space. This state requires the AI to fully adopt human values while simultaneously permitting our rapid extinction.

S3.rationale: Rapid, unaligned capability leaps in the 2030s provide a pathway for an AI to treat human survival as an instrumental obstacle. Logistical constraints of complete global extermination limit the likelihood of this occurring before the target date.

S4.rationale: Corporate and national races produce multiple independent, superintelligent systems that effectively marginalize human power. Fast takeoff dynamics prevent any single actor from establishing a monopoly before this competitive ecology solidifies.

S5.rationale: Establishing causally separated regions with independent human-AI structural states requires deep space colonization. The physical and economic constraints of space travel render this entirely impossible by 2040.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces face biological constraints, regulatory hurdles, and deployment logistics that prevent civilization-wide integration by 2040. True continuous uploading and radical biological redesign require timescales extending well beyond this target date.

S7.rationale: A rapidly advancing AI secures a decisive strategic advantage and manages humanity as a welfare or conservation project. In this state, humans survive comfortably but possess zero meaningful control over civilizational trajectories.

S8.rationale: Human institutions adapt to steady AI capability gains, integrating them as distinct but balancing powers. Economic dependencies and legal frameworks sustain a shared, multipolar power dynamic throughout the 2030s.

S9.rationale: Societal inertia, intense regulatory focus, and technological bottlenecks keep ultimate authority firmly in human hands. Traditional human power structures successfully constrain AI systems or capabilities simply remain below fully transformative levels.

S10.rationale: A dominant state or corporate actor leverages early artificial general intelligence to permanently freeze the geopolitical and technological balance. This singleton scenario materializes if one project achieves and ruthlessly defends a decisive strategic advantage.

S11.rationale: Global coordination to dismantle advanced compute infrastructure faces prohibitive game-theoretic obstacles among competing nations. Only an unprecedented, universally recognized near-miss catastrophe triggers this level of deliberate technological surrender.

S1.rationale: Extreme destructive capabilities could be unleashed by conflict or unaligned AI before multi-planetary resilience is achieved. The short timeframe limits the likelihood of total simultaneous annihilation.

S2.rationale: A scenario where AI perfectly retains human values while humans perish requires highly specific alignment successes paired with catastrophic physical failures. This narrow intersection of events is highly improbable by 2040.

S3.rationale: Rapid, unaligned capability gains could outpace defensive measures and institutional controls. An indifferent superintelligence could optimize Earth's resources for its own goals within a decade of its creation.

S4.rationale: Nation-states and megacorporations are heavily incentivized to deploy autonomous AI agents for economic and military supremacy. The resulting dynamic could easily become an entrenched competition where human oversight is marginalized by the speed of machine interactions.

S5.rationale: Establishing causally separated civilizations requires interstellar travel or extreme isolation capabilities. Physical and logistical constraints make this impossible to achieve by 2040.

S6.rationale: While brain-computer interfaces are advancing, strict biological constraints and clinical trial regulations will slow widespread adoption. True identity-continuous structural merger will remain localized rather than civilization-wide on this timeline.

S7.rationale: AI systems may cross a threshold where they manage complex infrastructure far better than humans, leading to a decisive power transfer. Humans would likely be kept comfortable but powerless under the administration of such systems.

S8.rationale: Economic and political structures will adapt aggressively to maintain human sovereignty alongside transformative AI. The 14-year horizon strongly favors a prolonged transitional period where neither biological humans nor machine systems completely dominate.

S9.rationale: Physical bottlenecks like energy grids, data scarcity, and hardware supply chains strongly favor gradual capability curves. Institutional forces will leverage these bottlenecks to heavily regulate AI, ensuring humans remain legally and practically in control.

S10.rationale: A first-mover in artificial general intelligence could secure a decisive strategic advantage and enforce a global freeze to prevent rivals from emerging. This requires a unipolar breakthrough that successfully overcomes international coordination failures.

S11.rationale: Giving up powerful AI requires unprecedented global coordination against massive economic and military incentives. Without a singleton enforcing it, rogue actors would immediately violate any international relinquishment treaties.

S1.rationale: Extreme destructive events, such as an AI-driven global conflict that accidentally wipes out the biosphere and its own infrastructure, are plausible but historically rare.

S2.rationale: An AI perfectly inheriting human values while humanity still completely goes extinct by 2040 requires a highly specific and unlikely sequence of events.

S3.rationale: If transformative AI arrives quickly and is fundamentally misaligned, an aggressive global resource grab could rapidly eliminate humanity.

S4.rationale: A rapid, multipolar takeoff could result in multiple competing superintelligent systems that marginalize human civilization before any single actor gains decisive control.

S5.rationale: Establishing causally separated human or AI civilizations, such as self-sustaining interstellar colonies, is physically impossible given the brief timeline to 2040.

S6.rationale: Deep brain-computer interfaces will advance, but achieving identity-continuous biological and machine integration as the dominant global structure by 2040 is severely constrained by medical realities.

S7.rationale: A single advanced AI or coalition could achieve a decisive strategic advantage and manage civilization, keeping humans alive but entirely disempowered.

S8.rationale: AI systems will likely become deeply capable autonomous actors, yet human states and corporations will possess enough physical capital and enforcement power to prevent total domination.

S9.rationale: Due to institutional inertia, massive physical infrastructure dependencies, and stringent regulatory frameworks, humans are highly likely to maintain ultimate oversight and control over AI by 2040.

S10.rationale: A first-mover AGI or state coalition might attempt to establish a global singleton to prevent competitors, though perfect global enforcement by 2040 remains extremely challenging.

S11.rationale: Permanent global coordination to dismantle and abandon advanced AI development is highly improbable given intense geopolitical competition and overwhelming economic incentives.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Fast extinction scenarios are technically possible but unlikely within a mere fourteen-year horizon. Physical constraints on weaponization and resource mobilization strongly limit global annihilation speed.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Humanity being completely replaced by a value-aligned AI successor within 14 years assumes both rapid capability gains and a flawlessly executed, yet fatal, handover.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: An unaligned AI takeover resulting in human extinction is physically and logistically constrained by the short timeframe. However, a rapid unaligned takeoff remains a non-zero tail risk.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Rapid proliferation of autonomous AI agents could outpace human institutional control, creating a multipolar machine-dominated economy. Energy constraints and hardware bottlenecks keep this probability moderate for the target date.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Establishing causally separated, self-sustaining off-world colonies by 2040 is physically and economically impossible. Space exploration currently lacks the trajectory for such rapid structural divergence.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Radical biological modification and neural uploading require neuroscientific breakthroughs far beyond 2040 timelines. Deep brain-computer interfaces will likely remain medical or niche rather than civilization-defining by this date.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A highly capable AI could rapidly assume control of critical infrastructure and governance for optimization or safety purposes. Humanity could comfortably or uncomfortably persist as wards of a system we can no longer govern.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: AI systems and human institutions will likely integrate as competing and cooperating sovereign entities. Economic incentives strongly favor empowering AIs while human legal frameworks fight to retain equivalent civilizational power.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Fourteen years is a short timeframe for a complete loss of civilizational control, keeping ultimate authority in human hands. Regulatory frameworks, hardware bottlenecks, and cautious deployment will keep AI functionally bounded.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: A dominant state coalition or a singular aligned AI establishes a global surveillance and enforcement regime to prevent the creation of unaligned models. This architecture imposes permanent structural stasis to preempt multipolar technological ruin.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Giving up transformative AI requires near-impossible global coordination against overwhelming economic incentives. Only an unprecedented, highly visible AI-driven catastrophe could trigger such universal relinquishment by 2040.
